review_notes: Read the whole file and grepped Mathlib for uses of rootsOfUnityAddChar, rootsOfUnityCircleEquiv, rootsOfUnitytoCircle, and injective_toCircle. The roots-of-unity declarations have no consumers outside this file. ZMod.toCircle and stdAddChar are already bundled as AddChars, and rootsOfUnityCircleEquiv is already a MulEquiv. rootsOfUnitytoCircle is already a MonoidHom, and ZMod.toCircle_addChar is bundled. The one real gap is that the bijectivity of rootsOfUnityAddChar is stated only as a separate Bijective fact, so the finding is moderate and its only consumers are in this file. I did not build or compile a replacement, and I did not look up the exact name or signature of the Mathlib constructor (probably MulEquiv.ofBijective or AddEquiv.ofBijective).

findings.problem: ZMod.rootsOfUnityAddChar is a bundled AddChar from ZMod n to rootsOfUnity n Circle. The file proves it is bijective, which makes it an isomorphism ZMod n ≃ μ_n. The isomorphism is exposed only as a Bijective fact about the underlying function. The same file works with the surjectivity half through the unbundled composite `rootsOfUnityCircleEquiv n ∘ ZMod.rootsOfUnityAddChar n`. Anyone who wants an equivalence, such as an inverse, a symm, or transport of structure, has to rebuild it from `Bijective` themselves.
findings.proposed_change: Bundle the bijection as a group isomorphism, for example `ZMod.rootsOfUnityAddEquiv n : Multiplicative (ZMod n) ≃* rootsOfUnity n Circle`, or the additive version into `Additive (rootsOfUnity n Circle)`. Build it from the existing AddChar's monoid hom and the proved bijectivity, using the standard `ofBijective` constructor. Keep `bijective_rootsOfUnityAddChar` as a corollary or as the construction input. Then state the composite with `rootsOfUnityCircleEquiv` as an equivalence composition (a `trans` of two equivalences) instead of `∘` on functions.
findings.benefit: Users get an inverse and a `symm` that identify the roots of unity in the circle with ZMod n. The composite with rootsOfUnityCircleEquiv becomes a composition of MulEquivs, so the bijectivity argument no longer needs the `Surjective.of_comp_left` plus injectivity juggling. The cost is one definition and its coercion lemma.

evidence.excerpt: noncomputable def rootsOfUnityCircleEquiv : rootsOfUnity n Circle ≃* rootsOfUnity n ℂ where
